item.title: New Linux Patches Allow More Easily Changing The Tux Kernel Boot Logo
item.description: A new patch series that was posted this week allow for users to more easily replace the default kernel boot logo. While many of us are long accustomed to seeing the picture of Tux as the kernel boot logo, for those preferring to better customize your console boot experience these patches allow it to be easily manipulated via the kernel configuration "Kconfig" options...

item.title: Linux Addressing Out-Of-Memory Killer Inaccuracy On Large Core Count Systems
item.description: A patch is on the way to the Linux kernel and looks like it could be ready for the 6.20~7.0 kernel for addressing out-of-memory "OOM" killer inaccuracy behavior when dealing with large core count systems...

item.title: Aeryn OS Continuing To Focus On Tooling & Infrastructure In 2026
item.description: The Aeryn OS Linux distribution formerly known as Serpent OS has published a 2025 retrospective to recap the project changes over the past year as well as a look ahead to 2026...

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.6 Fixes A Common Panel-Related Crash, Improves OpenBSD Support
item.description: KDE developer Nate Graham is out with the first issue of This Week in Plasma for 2026. Last week was a warning that This Week in Plasma could become less frequent without new volunteers to help takeover. Nate Graham announced that John Veness has stepped up to help co-author these weekly KDE development posts...

item.title: RADV Driver Lands Another Big Improvement For Early AMD GCN Graphics Cards
item.description: Beyond Linux 6.19 switching old AMD GCN 1.0 and 1.1 GPUs to the AMDGPU kernel driver by default for better performance, RADV out-of-the-box, and more, there are still more improvements planned for these aging AMD graphics cards. Timur Kristóf of Valve's Linux graphics team has been leading the effort to enhance the old graphics card support and on Friday night merged a big improvement for the RADV Vulkan driver in Mesa 26.0...

item.title: GNOME Glycin Adds XPM/XBM Support To Address Fedora's Last Unsandboxed Image Loader
item.description: GNOME's Glycin project as the Rust-based sandboxed and extendable image loading library now supports XPM and XBM images. This is notable since those formats were the last unsandboxed image loading formats used on Fedora Linux...

item.title: Stoolap 0.2 Released For Modern Embedded SQL Database In Rust
item.description: Stooplap v0.2 released today as this SQLite alternative for providing embedded SQL database needs while written in the Rust programming language. Stoolap supports both in-memory and persistent storage models...

item.title: Linux Audio Quirk Handling On The Way For Dell Panther Lake Laptops
item.description: Ahead of the initial batch of Intel Panther Lake laptops expected to be showcased at CES next week in Las Vegas, we're seeing last minute quirk updates for these products expected to soon come to market...

item.title: Box64 v0.4 Improves Support For DRM Protected Games, Steam Is Now More Stable
item.description: While Fex-Emu has been getting a lot of attention lately for being Valve-sponsored and powering the upcoming Steam Frame, Box64 continues making progress as another great open-source project for running x86_64 Linux binaries on AArch64 Linux as well as an eye on other architectures like RISC-V...

item.title: Rust-Based Fjall 3.0 Released For Key-Value Storage Engine Akin To RocksDB
item.description: In addition to the release of Stoolap 0.2 as a modern embedded SQL database written in Rust, Fjall 3.0 is available as another Rust-written database solution. Fjall is a log-structured, embedable key-value storage engine akin to RocksDB but with the benefit of being written in Rust. With Fjall 3.0 its performance is now very competitive...
